intro: つつ is the written counterpart of ながら: it attaches to a verb's ます-stem and keeps that action running alongside another. It has three uses: つつ "while", つつも "although" (one person acting against what they know or feel), and つつある "is in the process of", for a change that is under way. It attaches to verbs only.

skills.rule: Verb ます-stem + つつ: "while" (same subject); + つつも: "although"; + つつある: a change is steadily under way.
skills.explain:
Form: ます-stem + つつ. 考えます → 考えつつ, 楽しみます → 楽しみつつ, します → しつつ. Nouns and adjectives never take つつ.

つつ as "while" means the same as ながら but sounds written or formal. Both actions belong to the same subject, and the final verb is the main one: 景色を楽しみつつ歩いた.

つつも (or つつ alone, when the clash is obvious) means "although": the subject knows or feels X and still does Y. It is most common with verbs of knowing and feeling: 知りつつも, 悪いと思いつつ.

つつある marks a change in progress toward a new state: 増えつつある, 変わりつつある, 回復しつつある. It is used with change verbs, typically in news and reports. It is not a stylish ている: for someone simply in the middle of an activity (eating, reading) use ている.
patterns: [change verb ます-stem] つつある

examples.jp: 先生[せんせい]の話[はなし]を聞[き]き{つつ}、メモを取[と]った。
examples.en: I took notes while listening to the teacher.

examples.jp: 景色[けしき]を楽[たの]しみ{つつ}、ゆっくり歩[ある]いた。
examples.en: I walked slowly, enjoying the scenery.

examples.jp: 予算[よさん]を考[かんが]え{つつ}、計画[けいかく]を立[た]てる必要[ひつよう]がある。
examples.en: We need to make plans while keeping the budget in mind.

examples.jp: この町[まち]の人口[じんこう]は減[へ]り{つつ}ある。
examples.en: The population of this town is steadily shrinking.

examples.jp: 体[からだ]に悪[わる]いと知[し]り{つつも}、たばこがやめられない。
examples.en: Although I know it's bad for me, I can't give up smoking.

contrast.note: ながら is the everyday "while" and also takes adjectives and nouns for "although" (狭いながらも). つつ is written and takes verbs only.
て links actions in sequence or gives the manner: 座って話す. It does not by itself say that two actions run side by side the way つつ does.
ものの concedes a completed fact and allows two subjects: 薬を飲んだものの熱は下がらない. つつも is one person acting against what they know at the same time.

mistakes.bad: 彼[かれ]は若[わか]い{つつも}、とてもしっかりしている。
mistakes.good: 彼[かれ]は若[わか]い{ながらも}、とてもしっかりしている。
mistakes.note: つつ attaches only to verb stems; an adjective needs ながらも.

mistakes.bad: 今[いま]、ご飯[はん]を食[た]べ{つつ}あります。
mistakes.good: 今[いま]、ご飯[はん]を食[た]べ{て}います。
mistakes.note: つつある describes a gradual change, not an ordinary action in progress; use ている.

mistakes.bad: 母[はは]が料理[りょうり]し{つつ}、私[わたし]は掃除[そうじ]した。
mistakes.good: 母[はは]が料理[りょうり]している{あいだ}、私[わたし]は掃除[そうじ]した。
mistakes.note: Two different people: つつ needs one subject, so use 間.

skills.tip: つつ = written ながら, verbs only. つつも = "knowing that, yet". つつある = changing as we speak.
